results.text: The draft proposes replacing the current SQS event-transport topology with an EventBridge event bus named `widgets-events`, using rule-based routing so each consumer can attach through its own matching rule without producer changes or queue fan-out plumbing. This is proposed future direction only, not an accepted or implemented change.

results.text: The EventBridge transport proposal leaves three questions unresolved: the cost of EventBridge at current event volume versus three flat queues; whether `event_version` belongs in `detail-type` or the event body; and whether migration should use a dual-publish window or a hard cutover.

Every widget queue must have a dead-letter queue. Messages must move to the DLQ after 5 receives, configured as `maxReceiveCount: 5`. The visibility timeout must be `90 seconds` on all widget queues. | When: Saturday, August 1, 2026, as a requirement established by the event-transport specification; the requirements are ongoing for all widget queues | Involving: Widget-event producers and consumers, Amazon SQS, and the operators responsible for configuring and monitoring the queues | The dead-letter-queue requirement provides a defined failure path for messages that cannot be successfully processed after repeated receives. The exact threshold, `maxReceiveCount: 5`, makes failure handling actionable and deterministic. The `90 seconds` visibility timeout controls how long a received message remains hidden from other consumers before it can be delivered again.

results.text: Under the proposed EventBridge design, producers would publish to `widgets-events` with `detail-type` set to the event class; consumers would declare matching EventBridge rules and continue consuming from per-consumer SQS queues; EventBridge would route matching events to those queues, preserving SQS-based consumer retry and DLQ semantics. These are proposed contracts, not accepted or implemented interfaces.

As of August 20, 2026, the EventBridge transport proposal remains a draft and no transport decision has changed. Amazon SQS standard queues remain the accepted and authoritative transport for widget processing under `spec.eventing.transport.0001`, using one queue per event class.
